slides.title: A claim about a population
slides.body: A hypothesis test uses sample evidence to assess a claim about a population parameter.
slides.question: Does a claim about average processing time concern μ or the observed sample mean?

slides.title: The null hypothesis
slides.body: The null hypothesis specifies the population claim assessed as the reference model.
slides.question: For a claimed mean processing time of 12 minutes, how could we write H₀?

slides.title: The alternative hypothesis
slides.body: The alternative describes the population change or difference for which we seek evidence.
slides.question: If the question is whether the mean exceeds 12 minutes, how should Hₐ be written?

slides.title: Direction of the question
slides.body: A one-sided alternative specifies a direction; a two-sided alternative allows either direction.
slides.question: Which alternative matches a question about any change from μ=12?

slides.title: Choosing before looking
slides.body: The research question should determine the alternative before inspecting the outcome.
slides.question: What problem arises if we choose the tail only after seeing whether the sample mean is high or low?

slides.title: The null sampling model
slides.body: Under H₀, a sampling model describes the statistic's variation if the null claim holds.
slides.question: Why should this model concern sample means rather than individual processing times?

slides.title: A test statistic
slides.body: A test statistic summarizes how far sample evidence departs from the null model.
slides.question: Why should distance from the null value be judged relative to standard error?

slides.title: An assumption check
slides.body: A valid test relies on the sampling design and the assumptions of its probability model.
slides.question: Could a very small p-value repair a strongly biased sample?

slides.title: The p-value
slides.body: A p-value is the null-model probability of results at least as extreme as observed, in the direction of the alternative.
slides.question: Which assumption about H₀ is used when calculating it?

slides.title: One tail or two?
slides.body: Synthetic result: the sample mean is above the null mean. The alternative is two-sided.
slides.question: Would considering only equally high sample means capture all results at least as extreme?

slides.title: A p-value is not a hypothesis probability
slides.body: Synthetic result: a valid test reports p-value=0.03.
slides.question: Does this assign a 3% probability to H₀ being true?

slides.title: Significance level
slides.body: The significance level α sets the rejection rule and controls the Type I error rate under a valid test.
slides.question: Why should α be chosen before examining the p-value?

slides.title: A rejection decision
slides.body: Synthetic valid test: p-value=0.03; significance level α=0.05.
slides.question: What decision follows for H₀?

slides.title: A nonrejection decision
slides.body: Synthetic valid test: p-value=0.18; significance level α=0.05.
slides.question: Does failing to reject H₀ establish that it is true?

slides.title: Type I error
slides.body: A Type I error rejects a null hypothesis that is true.
slides.question: If H₀ states that mean processing time is 12 minutes, what would a Type I error conclude?

slides.title: Type II error
slides.body: A Type II error fails to reject a null hypothesis that is false.
slides.question: If the true mean exceeds 12 minutes, what would a Type II error miss?

slides.title: Power
slides.body: Power is the probability of rejecting H₀ for a specified alternative that is true.
slides.question: How might a larger sample help detect a small departure from the null value?

slides.title: Statistical and practical importance
slides.body: A small p-value measures evidence against a null model, rather than the size or importance of the difference.
slides.question: Could a 0.02-minute difference be statistically significant but operationally unimportant?

slides.title: An interval connection
slides.body: For matching two-sided mean procedures, a 95% confidence interval excluding μ₀ corresponds to rejecting H₀:μ=μ₀ at α=0.05.
slides.question: Would a matching interval from 12.2 to 12.8 reject a null mean of 12?

slides.title: A careful conclusion
slides.body: Synthetic valid test rejects H₀:μ=12 in favor of Hₐ:μ>12.
slides.question: How would you state the evidence without claiming proof or explaining why the mean changed?
